back: Rate of flow of thermal energy per unit area per unit temperature gradient: k = (Q/t)x/(AΔθ). Unit W m⁻¹ K⁻¹.
All solids: lattice vibrations passed between neighbours. Metals: also fast free electrons, which dominate.
No side losses → same Q/t through every section → uniform gradient, straight temperature-distance line.
Side losses → Q/t decreases along the bar → gradient decreases: curve below the lagged line.
Same rate of flow through each layer; the layer with the largest x/(kA) takes the largest temperature drop.

front: Typical k values / W m⁻¹ K⁻¹
back: Copper ~390, steel ~50, glass ~0.8, brick ~0.6, wood ~0.15, polystyrene ~0.03, still air ~0.025.
Searle: long, thick, lagged bar for good conductors. Lees: thin, wide disc for poor conductors.
Air conducts very poorly; trapping it in small pockets prevents convection.
